title: Workstation Setup
content: Finally got around to imaging the new machine this weekend. Went with Arch + i3wm, feels snappy. I ended up naming it Atlas-Desk because it holds everything and I liked the mythology angle. Still need to migrate my dotfiles from the old rig.

title: Typing Practice
content: Decided to shake up my muscle memory a bit. I've been on QWERTY for 15 years but the wrist strain is real lately. Started practicing Colemak this month — 20 minute sessions every morning. Down to about 28 WPM which is humbling. Hoping to break 60 by end of month.

title: Editor Preferences
content: After going back and forth on dark vs light themes I'm sticking with Solarized Light for now. Better for daylight hours and my eyes don't feel as tired after long sessions. Using it in both VS Code and Neovim. Will probably try something new next quarter.

title: Travel Choice
content: Been going back and forth between Amsterdam and Rotterdam for the hackathon. Amsterdam felt too touristy and pricey. Rotterdam won — better venue options, cheaper accommodation and I've never been. Flights are booked for the third week of May. Super hyped.

title: Side Project Name
content: Spent an hour just brainstorming names for this thing. Went through Beacon, Ember, Flare, Moth before landing on Lantern — it captures the idea of something guiding you in the dark without being too cute. Going with Project Lantern as the working title. Will revisit before any public release.

title: Writing Stack
content: Tried about a dozen options in Obsidian before finalizing my writing setup. Rejected Palatino (too common), Lora (nice but too round), and Libre Baskerville (serifs too heavy). Settled on EB Garamond for long-form drafts — the optical sizing at 14px is genuinely lovely. Might do a blog post about this rabbit hole.

title: Git Workflow
content: Standardizing git conventions across my personal repos. Dropping master and main — too many projects use both interchangeably and it causes merge confusion. Going with mainline as the default base branch name going forward. Updated my git config template and added a note in the onboarding doc.

title: Meeting Routine
content: Trying to improve how I show up in planning meetings. Changed the habit of bringing coffee since it makes me too jittery to listen well. Switched to ginger tea — warm, settling, no caffeine spike. Team calls have genuinely felt better. Small change but worth noting.

title: Assistant Persona
content: Set up a local LLM instance with a persona config. Considered Aria, Lyra, Iris, and Echo. Went with Nova in the end — feels energetic but not tryhard. Updated the system prompt and the TTS voice label. Runs well on the local rig.

title: Schedule Habit
content: Finally blocked off dedicated deep-work time in my calendar after months of constant interruptions. Monday is too chaotic with standup cascades. Wednesday has too many recurring check-ins. Thursday turned out to be the cleanest — no team rituals, low Slack traffic. Blocking it as a no-meeting, no-chat day indefinitely.

title: Language Learning Goals
content: Picked Rust for this quarter after getting frustrated with memory management in C++. Been working through The Book for the past few weeks and it's starting to click. The compiler is strict but fair — reminds me to be more careful about ownership. Building a small CLI tool as practice. Pair of good resources: Learning Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists (hilarious) and the Rustlings exercises.

title: Secondary Machine Config
content: Rebuilt the backup laptop over the weekend. Arch was getting stale after 18 months. Decided to try NixOS this time since I've been hearing good things about reproducible configs. Learning curve is steep but the idea of declarative system config is incredibly appealing. Set up flakes and now my entire environment is version controlled. If it breaks I can just roll back to a known state.

title: Knowledge Management System
content: After 3 years of scattered notes across Notion, Bear, and plain markdown files I finally committed to building something cohesive. Named it Cerebral (bit pretentious but I like it). It's a personal wiki with bidirectional linking, tagging, and full-text search. Keeps everything in a Git repo so I don't need to trust some SaaS provider. Been migrating old notes in and it feels weirdly cathartic to organize everything.

title: Weekly Tech Podcast
content: Been listening to Syntax for about 8 months now. Wes and Scott keep me up to date on web dev trends without the 2-hour commitment of other podcasts. Their hot takes are chaotic but always thoughtful. I like how they break down new frameworks and tools with actual depth. The Discord community is surprisingly helpful too. Monday mornings while running is the perfect time slot for it.

title: Web Framework Selection
content: New project is getting SvelteKit. After using Next.js for 4 projects, I wanted something different. Svelte's reactivity model is actually elegant and SvelteKit's design feels less magic-heavy than Next. Built-in routing through file structure, form actions, and proper SSR support. Early days but I'm really enjoying how it pushes you toward better patterns naturally. Probably going to stick with this for a while unless something radically better emerges.
